body:
The word "vaporizer" covers a wide family of devices, from a sealed disposable that costs under twenty dollars to a large adjustable mod with replaceable batteries. For a newcomer, the names can be confusing: disposable, pod, pen, mod, tank, box, stick. This guide sorts the main types of vape devices sold today, explains how each works, who each suits, what to look for, what upkeep each needs, how they compare in cost and simplicity and how to choose. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice. We make no health claims.

## The main types at a glance
- **Disposable vapes:** sealed devices, pre-filled and used until empty.
- **Closed pod systems:** a rechargeable battery with pre-filled pods you swap.
- **Refillable pod systems:** a rechargeable battery with pods you fill yourself.
- **Vape pens:** slim, pen-shaped devices with a small tank.
- **Tank and mod systems:** an adjustable battery unit and a refillable tank.
- **Box mods:** larger, rectangular, powerful versions of the above.
- **Other formats:** pouches and devices sold under newer ingredient labels.

## Disposable vapes
A disposable contains a battery, a coil and liquid in one sealed unit. You use it until the liquid or battery is finished, then recycle it. Many are rechargeable, and a large catalog of flavors exists, including more than 1,100 in ours. They suit people who want zero setup. Look at puff count, strength, rechargeability and size. See [how to choose a disposable vape](/blog/how-to-choose-a-disposable-vape/) and [puff counts explained](/blog/puff-count-explained/).

## Closed pod systems
A closed pod system has a reusable battery and pods that click in. The pods are pre-filled and sealed. When a pod is empty, you replace it. These are compact, simple and leak-resistant. They suit people who want flavor variety without filling liquid. See [what is a pod vape](/blog/what-is-a-pod-vape-and-how-to-choose/).

## Refillable pod systems
Like closed pods, but you fill the pod with your own liquid. Running costs are lower, and you can choose from many liquids. You must learn to fill, prime and avoid leaks. They suit people who want more choice and are happy to maintain the device. See [how to fill a pod without leaks](/blog/how-to-fill-a-pod-without-leaks/).

## Vape pens
Pens are slim devices with a built-in battery and a small tank. They are older in design, and they have mostly been replaced by pod systems, but some remain popular. They need coil changes and refilling, and they usually have a single button.

## Tank and mod systems
A mod holds batteries and electronics, and a tank holds liquid and a coil. You can adjust power and airflow, and choose from many coils and liquids. They suit people who want control. They need more learning and upkeep. See [what is a box mod](/blog/what-is-a-box-mod/).

## Box mods
Box mods are the larger end of the tank and mod family, often with dual batteries, high power and a screen. They suit enthusiasts. They need correctly rated batteries and careful handling. See [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

## Comparing them
In simplicity, disposables lead, then closed pods, refillable pods, pens, and finally mods. In running cost, mods and refillable pods lead, because they use liquid and coils. In control, mods lead. In portability, small disposables and pods lead. In waste, disposables produce the most electronic waste. In flavor choice, refillable systems offer the most, and closed pods and disposables offer plenty of ready-made options.

## What to look for in any device
- A reputable maker and clear labeling.
- A stated nicotine strength.
- USB-C charging on rechargeable devices.
- Protection against short circuits and overheating.
- Clear instructions.
- Availability of pods or coils, for systems that use them.

## Upkeep by type
Disposables need charging only. Closed pods need pod swaps and charging. Refillable pods need filling, coil or pod changes and cleaning. Mods need coil changes, cleaning, battery care and checking. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/) and [how to change a pod or coil](/blog/how-to-change-a-pod-or-coil/).

## Choosing by habit
If you use a device occasionally, a small disposable is enough. If you use it daily, a large rechargeable disposable or a pod system is better value. If you like to tinker, a mod suits. If you travel, compact devices are easier, and you must carry them in hand baggage. See [best vapes for travel](/blog/best-vapes-for-travel/).

## A worked example
A customer wants a first device and uses nicotine about twenty times a day, at home and at work. They consider a 5,000-puff disposable at $13.99, a 30,000-puff rechargeable at $18.99 and a refillable pod kit at $25. At about 200 puffs a day, the small disposable lasts 25 days and the large one lasts 150 days. The large disposable works out to roughly $0.13 a day. The pod kit costs more at first, but liquid and pods cost about $18 a month. The customer chooses the large disposable, with a second flavor for variety. The decision came from a few numbers, not from a name.

## Compliance and rules
All devices are for adults aged 21 and over. Adult signature is required on delivery, and some states restrict flavors or types. Check the rules where you live. See [state and local vape laws explained](/blog/state-and-local-vape-laws-explained/).

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### What is the difference between a vape and a vaporizer?
In everyday use, the words overlap. "Vaporizer" is a broader word, and "vape" usually means a nicotine device.

### Which type is cheapest?
It depends on use. Large disposables are cheap per puff, and refillable systems are cheap per month.

### Which type is easiest?
Disposables and closed pods.

### Which type is most flexible?
Tank and mod systems.

### Can I switch types later?
Yes. Many adults start simple and move on if they want more.

## Shop
Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/), [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and [vaporizers](/shop/vaporizers/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Other categories you may see
Some product pages use terms that overlap with the types above. "Starter kit" usually means a battery, a tank or pod and a charger, sold together for a first purchase. "All-in-one" means the battery, tank and coil are built together, often a pen-style device. "Pod mod" means a pod system with adjustable power, between a simple pod and a mod. "Squonk mod" refers to a bottom-feeding mod with a squeezable bottle, for experienced users. "Rebuildable" devices let users build their own coils, and they are for experts who understand battery safety and electrical theory. If you meet a term you do not know, ask us before you buy, through the [contact page](/contact/).

## Disposables compared with refillable systems in more detail
A refillable system costs more at first and less over time, and it asks more of you: filling, priming, coil changes and cleaning. It rewards you with a wider choice of liquids, more control over strength and the ability to repair or replace parts. A disposable costs more per puff over a long period, and asks nothing of you. It rewards you with simplicity. Think about which you would honestly prefer in a busy week. A system that you do not look after is worse than a disposable you use happily.

## Size and weight
Size affects where you carry a device and how it feels. Small disposables and pods slip into a pocket and weigh little. Large disposables, with big batteries, can be about the size of a small flashlight. Mods are the largest. If you carry a device in a pocket all day, size matters, and a heavy device can be tiring. Check the dimensions on the product page, and compare with something you know, such as a phone or a pen.

## Battery and charging by type
Disposables have built-in batteries, and rechargeable ones charge through USB-C. Pod systems have built-in batteries, and charge by cable. Mods use removable cells, charged in the device or in an external charger. Charging times vary from about thirty minutes for a small pod device to a few hours for a large disposable. Use a standard 5V adapter and a good cable, on a hard surface, and do not leave devices charging unattended. See [how to charge a disposable](/blog/how-to-charge-a-disposable/) and [how to extend vape battery life](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/).

## Replacement parts
Parts are a practical point that often gets forgotten. For pods, check that the pods are widely stocked. For tanks, check that coils are sold in your area. For mods, check that batteries and chargers are easy to find. If the maker stops supporting a line, your device may become hard to use. We stock [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for many of the systems we sell, and we list compatibility on the product page.

## A decision guide in words
- **I want the simplest option:** a disposable.
- **I want variety without filling:** a closed pod system.
- **I want lower running costs and liquid choice:** a refillable pod system.
- **I want control and big vapor:** a tank and mod system, after learning the basics.
- **I want no device at all:** consider a pouch. See [nicotine delivery options compared](/blog/nicotine-delivery-options-compared/).

## Final advice
Start simple, learn what you like and change one thing at a time. Read labels, keep devices away from children and pets, charge carefully and recycle devices properly. Nicotine is addictive, and products are for adults aged 21 and over.

faq.q: What are the main types of vapes?
faq.a: Disposables, closed pod systems, refillable pod systems, pens, tank and mod systems and box mods.

faq.q: Which type is easiest to start with?
faq.a: A disposable or a closed pod kit, because neither needs filling or settings.

faq.q: Which type has the lowest running cost?
faq.a: Refillable pod and tank systems, because they use liquid and coils instead of replacing the whole device.

faq.q: Which type gives the most control?
faq.a: Tank and mod systems, with adjustable power and airflow.

faq.q: Which type makes the most waste?
faq.a: Disposables. All devices with batteries should be recycled properly.
Yes. Many adults start with a simple device and move on if they want more control or lower costs.
